description.narrative: The National Coalition of Human Rights Defenders - Kenya (NCHRD eller Defenders Coalition) är en medlemsorganisation etablerad 2007 och registrerad i Kenya som en stiftelse. Defenders Coalition arbetar primärt med skydd av människorättsförsvarare i Kenya. Bland annat innebär deras arbete att starka kapaciteten av människorättsförsvarare för att arbeta mer effektivt, samtidigt som de arbetar med påverkansarbete för bättre lagstiftning och institutionell miljö för att minska människorättsförsvarare sårbarhet för förföljelse och/eller skada. Ambassaden bidrar med kärnstöd till Defenders Coalition Strategiska Plan 2022-2025 - Safety. Security. Wellbeing of Rights Defenders.

The National Coalition of Human Rights Defenders - Kenya (NCHRD or Defenders Coalition) is a national membership organization established in 2007 and registered under Kenyan law as a Trust. The Defenders Coalition works primarily for the protection of Human Rights Defenders (HRDs) in Kenya. Among others, the Defenders Coalition strengthens capacities of HRDs to work more effectively, besides advocating for favorable legal, policy and institutional environments in order to reduce their vulnerability to the risk of persecution and or harm. The Embassy provide core-support to the Defenders Coalition Strategic Plan 2020-2025 - Safety. Security. Wellbeing of Rights Defenders.

The overall objective is Enhancing the Safety, Security and Wellbeing of Human Rights Defenders.
Key results areas and specific objectives are:
I. Supportive and enabling norms, policies and institutional frameworks that enhance security, work and wellbeing of HRDs adopted
Objective 1: To influence the development of new legislation and policy solutions for protecting human rights defenders including environmental, women, indigenous people, youth, PWDs, journalists & LGBTQI from retaliation, by building the capacity of HRDs and their allies to conduct effective legislative advocacy campaigns and fostering collaborative networks.
Objective 2: To contribute to enhanced enabling environment/ civic space for HRDs through promoting positive public perceptions/attitude change towards HRDs and their work
II. Effective protection response to and safe working envrionment for diverse HRDs at risk delivered in a timely and appropriate manner
Objective: To improve the provision of sustainable & effective services for human rights defenders through building the capacity of legal professionals through skills building and supporting legal professionals engaging in strategic litigation.
III. Socie-economic wellbeing for HRDs improved for increased civic engagement, passionate and accountable protection for human rights
Objective: To promote awareness on mental health to eliminate stigma and encourage HRDs to seek interventions and promote social recognition and celebration of the work and resilience of HRDs.
IV. Defenders Coalition consolidates its position as a 'dynamic, relevant, effective and resilient institution'
Objective: To strengthen the institutional capacity to implement its mandate efficiently and effectively through strengthening of internal systems and structures.
The key results areas are consistent with the Defenders Coalition Strategi Plan 2020-2025

The following are some of the key results/ achievements from 2023 annual report:
1. Improved legal and policy environment
Defenders Coalition work has positively impacted the legal and policy environment to better safeguard the work of HRDs. Notably, the Office of Director of Public Prosecutions (ODPP) withdrew criminal charges against HRDs when it was pointed out to them that they were unwarranted or framed charges.
Defenderes Coaliation also celebrated precedent-setting court ruling that limits future arrests of HRDs without the express authorization of the Director of Public Prosecution. This was the result of Defenders Coalition's legal intervention when a land and environment HRDs was targeted for multiple arrests and prosecution of framed up charges because of their campaign against encroachment on community land by a private salt extractive company. These victories are not only precedent setting but also have significantly reduced the risks of persecution and harm faced by HRDs in Kenya.
During the period, the Defenders Coalition increased its engagement with the duty bearers to strengthen good working relationships especially with the justice actors under the Court Users Committee Platform in several counties. The engagements were informed by recommendations of various assessments that recommended engagement with critical justice actors to mitigate the current prevailing risks faced by HRDs, as well as the need to have more engagements. Moving forward Defenders Coalition shall leverage links with the judiciary to create awareness of the role that HRDs play in the society and their criminalization.
Defenders Coalition's presence at the African Commission for Human and Peoples Rights(ACPHR) directly or through their regional partners has continued to push for the recognition of HRDs work and development of supportive policies and programs. Defenders Coalition prioritized amplifying the voices of marginalized groups, environmental defenders, and gender minorities groups. Defenders Coalition facilitated the participation of 10 women human rights defenders' at the ACHPR and to directly engage with the commission about their concerns.
2. Enhanced risk mitigation and response
The Defenders Coalition remained committed to enhancing risk mitigation measures and respond in a timely manner to HRDs at risk. Towards this goal, Defenders Coalition provided a broad spectrum of protection interventions and services to HRDs at risk. Capacity building training for three hundred and thirteen (313) to equip them with security training to navigate the risk that they encounter when they conduct their human rights work was conducted. Additional eighteen (18) HRDs were equipped with Train of Trainer skills to continuously support the HRDs in their communities. This, coupled with the improvement of enhancing organisational security for civil society organizations, has created a more conducive operating environment for human rights work. The team's trainees further accessed mental health support to enhance their well-being and resilience in the face of challenges.
3. Timely response to support those at risk
Defenders Coalition has remained the only national human rights organization that consistently and speedily responds to those that are faced with risks. A robust case management system enhanced NCHRD's documentation, case assessment and referral to a well coordinated network of legal, medical and psychosocial service providers. The interventions included: 115 legal representation, 208 relocation support, 9 organization security enhancement, 12 legal accompaniment, 14 medical support This totaled to 486 protection support to HRDs against a target of 250 during the period. In addition, Defenders Coalition facilitated increased uptake of psychosocial services and debriefings for HRDs.
4. Increased visibility and risk management through networking and partnership
The HRD Awards have gained popularity as an annual event that recognises through Awards, the extraordinary work of defending human rights. By embracing collective action of civil society and various missions members of the HRD Working group to hold the annual celebratory event to regularly discuss and action intervention to improve the HRD environment has been an added protective defense strategy for HRDs. Defenders Coalition plans to advance the spirit of the event and to regularly evaluate and incorporate lessons from past events to improve on the growth and visibility of HRDs Award 2024.
5. Institutional Development and Corporate Governance
Defenders Coalition invested heavily in enhancing its human resources capacity, policies, systems and governance. This was guided by the detailed recommendation of a Systems Audit conducted in 2021 that proposed several measures to strengthen corporate governance structures, human resources management, and administrative and coordination capacity. Defenders Coalition is implementing policies developed like Human Resource Management Policy, Procurement policy, and Board Policy. The policies shall be regularly assessed for review to enhance smooth operation and application.
Defenders Coalition has further increased its staff complement from fifteen to eighteen that has included line managers to lead various programmes. This has offset a heavy burden on the lead staff that implemented programmes despite increased demand. Defenders Coalition is keen to increase the use of technology in human resource, finance and administration management while also strengthening risk management as they adopt technology.
Their commitment to ensure sustainability of the Defenders Coalition is still on course. During the year, they held Climb for Justice hiking events in different parts of the country . Such activities help fundraise to set up Haki Village but also build solidarity among HRDs. Defenders Coalition has intentionally reached out to more donors to widen the support base. They successfully attracted funding from two additional funders, namely Mott Foundation and Hivos.
These achievements reflect the organization's commitment to creating a supportive environment for HRDs, upholding their rights in the pursuit of social justice and human rights and sustainability of Defenders Coalition work.
